[raw subtype: complete male epispadias] B: The caption explicitly identifies this clinical photograph as complete female epispadias within the exstrophy-epispadias complex. [raw subtype: classic bladder exstrophy] D: The caption directly identifies the panel as cloacal exstrophy, and the image clearly demonstrates a large exposed bladder plate with associated external tract malformation. [raw subtype: cloacal exstrophy]

in_text_mentions: inal tracts, musculoskeletal system, pelvic floor musculature, and bony pelvis. The three most common presentations of EEC are epispadias, classic bladder exstrophy (CBE), and cloacal exstrophy (CE) (Figure 1). Complete epispadias is the least severe form of EEC and presents with a dorsally open urethral meatus with mild pubic diastasis and a closed anterior abdominal wall and bladder. CBE, the most common presentation of EEC, presents with a wide pubic diastasis and an abdominal wall defect exposing an open bladder and urethra with an epispadiac opening.
